title: Currying dg-module diagrams over a tensor product
statement: Use the cochain-complex and dg-category conventions of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], the module Hom-complex conventions of [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution], and the enriched diagram conventions of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model], in sufficiently large universes. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal D$ be small dg categories over $\mathbf Z$. Let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal D)$ be covariant dg functors $\mathcal D\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$; a degree-$r$ transformation $\eta:F\to G$ satisfies $G(\delta)\eta_d=(-1)^{r|\delta|}\eta_{d'}F(\delta)$ and has differential $d\eta=d_G\eta-(-1)^r\eta d_F$. Define $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal D$ to have object pairs, morphism complexes $\mathcal A(a,a')\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathcal D(d,d')$, the tensor differential, and composition $(\beta\otimes\epsilon)\circ(\alpha\otimes\delta)=(-1)^{|\epsilon||\alpha|}(\beta\alpha\otimes\epsilon\delta)$ on homogeneous morphisms. There is an isomorphism of dg categories between strict dg functors $\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal D)$ and covariant dg modules over $\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal D$. It sends $F$ to $H$ with $H(a,d)=F(a)(d)$ and $H(\alpha\otimes\delta)=F(\alpha)_{d'}F(a)(\delta)$, and identifies all transformation complexes, differentials, identities and compositions. It identifies objectwise quasi-isomorphisms and objectwise degreewise surjections, and the projective model structures (hence cofibrant objects) on both sides whenever these structures exist.
